metadata.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Backport vllm-project/vllm#63475, #62936, #62467, #49139: persistent_topk radix CTA syncs, float4 tail lanes, radix histogram ring
metadata.body:
## Purpose

Backports of four upstream fixes to the persistent top-k kernel in csrc/persistent_topk.cuh, in the same form as the earlier backports (#657, #1406). main does not have them. The sparse indexers select through torch.ops._C.persistent_topk in decode: DeepSeek-V4 and DeepSeek-V3.2 (SparseAttnIndexer, vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py), GLM-5.3-Flash (vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py), and Qwen4Exp QSA calls it as well. On V100 (96 KiB opt-in shared memory per block) and RTX 8000 (64 KiB), launch_persistent_topk in csrc/libtorch_stable/topk.cu never takes the FilteredTopK route, which needs 128 KiB, so every decode batch runs persistent_topk_kernel, also above 32 rows. The kernel is built into _C_stable_libtorch, which needs a rebuild.

vllm-project/vllm#63475 ([Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: sync the CTA around radix barrier arrivals, upstream commit 3090266d8, by Andreas Karatzas). radix_topk lets thread 0 alone arrive at the inter-CTA barrier of each radix round. Without a CTA barrier first, it can arrive while other warps of its CTA are still adding their local histogram into the group's global histogram, or, on CTA 0, still zeroing the next round's buffer. Peer CTAs then read an incomplete histogram, pick a different pivot and emit duplicate or missing indices. Rows longer than RADIX_THRESHOLD (32768) take this path; for the C4 indexer of DeepSeek-V4 and the kpool indexer of GLM-5.3-Flash (kpool 4) that is a context above about 131k tokens. Upstream's reproduction (MI355X, HIP port of the kernel) found 146 wrong rows in 882,700 with neither barrier and none once the pre-arrival barrier is in. The one-line hunk applies unchanged. Upstream added no test because the race depends on warp scheduling. This PR adds test_persistent_topk_radix_rows_match_reference as a correctness guard for the radix path, not as a deterministic reproducer: rows of 32769 to 163843 entries (mostly not multiples of 4), k 512 and 2048, random scores, 256-value ties and all-equal rows, row strides for chunk-load vector widths 4, 2 and 1, and 1, 8 or 32 rows. Each case launches the kernel eight times and checks every row strictly against torch.topk: indices in range and unique, sorted selected values equal to the reference, and nothing written past the last row.

vllm-project/vllm#62936 ([2/N][Bugfix] Make persistent TopK exact on candidate overflow, upstream commit 33a73daf1, by Roberto L. Castro), only its end-of-row __syncthreads(). radix_topk ends with the tie loop, in which each thread scans shared_ordered for entries equal to the pivot, and returned without a CTA barrier. A CTA that owns several rows then starts its next row while slower warps are still in that loop: the next radix row's chunk load overwrites shared_ordered, and on CTA 0 the short-row path (histogram_2048_topk) zeroes and reuses the same dynamic shared memory, so the slow warps miss or misplace tied indices of the previous row. A CTA group gets several rows when there are fewer groups than rows. topk.cu caps the shared memory per CTA at 48 KiB for 5 to 8 rows (and at 35968 B for up to 4 rows), so wide rows give fewer groups than rows, for example 8 rows (one request with 7 draft tokens) that are 131072 entries wide: 6 groups on a V100 and 5 on an RTX 8000 (computed from the grid sizing in topk.cu, not measured). The rest of #62936 (exact selection on candidate overflow, two new headers) is not taken: it builds on vllm-project/vllm#59645 (topk_histogram_4096.cuh), which main does not have. The barrier belongs with #63475: its description names both barriers, and its merged diff carries only the pre-arrival one because #62936 had landed the end-of-row one a few hours earlier. The hunk and its comment are the upstream ones.

vllm-project/vllm#62467 ([Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length, upstream commit bde4d0011, by simon-veitner-redhat). histogram_2048_topk loads a row in float4 vectors and fills the lanes of the last vector that lie past seq_len with -inf. The collection pass treated those lanes like real entries, so when fewer than k scores of a row lie above the fp16 -inf bin, the threshold falls into that bin, the padding lanes are buffered as candidates, and the refinement reads and may select indices >= seq_len. The path runs for rows with k < length <= 8192, about 2k to 32k tokens of context for the C4 and kpool indexers. It needs a row with fewer than k scores above the fp16 -inf bin; whether the SM70 indexer scorers produce such rows is not known to us, so on our side this is hardening, and with finite scores the change has no effect. The kernel hunk applies unchanged. Upstream's test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail is taken as is, except that it calls the op through this file's new _run_persistent_topk helper instead of upstream's _run_topk_backend, which this tree does not have. Upstream reports for this test on B300: main 36 failed, 12 passed (every case whose length is not a multiple of 4 fails), with the fix 48 passed.

vllm-project/vllm#49139 ([Bugfix][Kernel] Fix persistent top-k histogram reuse after short rows, upstream commit e62abc37d, by xiao feng). radix_topk picks its triple-buffered global histogram by global_round = iter * 4 + round, where iter counts every row the CTA group visits, short rows included. A radix row leaves only the buffer of the next radix round clean. If the group's next radix row comes after a short row, its round 0 adds onto the stale counts of the earlier row, so every CTA derives the same wrong pivot and the row's top-k is wrong. The fix counts radix rows separately (radix_iter) in persistent_topk_kernel. It needs a CTA group that processes a long row, a short row and another long row in one launch: more than twice as many rows as groups, with rows above and below 32768 entries, e.g. several concurrent requests of which some have more than about 131k tokens of context. Our single-request deployment does not reach it; it is in this PR because it is the same kernel and the same rebuild. Upstream patched csrc/libtorch_stable/persistent_topk.cuh; the hunks apply unchanged to csrc/persistent_topk.cuh, and with this PR radix_topk is identical to upstream's at 3090266d8. Upstream's test_persistent_topk_reused_group_after_short_row is taken over with three changes: it calls the op through _run_persistent_topk instead of _run_topk_backend, it reads the properties of the current device instead of device 0, and it drops set_default_device("cuda:0"), since topk.cu sizes the grid from the current device and all tensors already name it. With main's topk.cu it builds 9 groups of 8 CTAs on a V100 and 8 groups of 8 CTAs on an RTX 8000 (27 and 24 rows, computed), so group 0 gets a long, a short and a long row. The length clamp that upstream later added to the same loop with vllm-project/vllm#51538 (negative lengths of padded MTP decode slots) is a separate fix and not part of this PR.

Not a duplicate: I searched the open and closed PRs and issues of this repository for 63475, 62936, 62467, 49139, 51538, persistent_topk, "persistent topk", radix_topk, "radix top-k", "topk histogram" and "top-k race"; none backports these fixes, and no open PR touches csrc/persistent_topk.cuh, csrc/libtorch_stable/topk.cu or tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py. Upstream, #64138 (BF16 logits in persistent top-k, a performance change) and the open #63847 (ROCm port) refer to these PRs and are not needed for them.

AI assistance was used for this backport. I reviewed every line and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

Rebuild _C_stable_libtorch, then on a Tesla V100 and on a Quadro RTX 8000:
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "reused_group or radix_rows_match or masked_row_tail"
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k persistent_topk
The same -k "reused_group or radix_rows_match or masked_row_tail" with this branch's test file, run from a main c98a8d664 checkout with main's _C_stable_libtorch (the new cases against main's kernel), on both GPUs
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py --collect-only
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD; pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD

## Path coverage

| Path / provider | Format | Key conditions (shape, TP/EP, graph, capability) | Expected selection / fallback | Evidence (source / static / executed / measured) | Unverified scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| radix_topk in persistent_topk_kernel, rows longer than 32768 | fp32 logits, k 512 / 1024 / 2048 | one multi-CTA group per row; V100 and RTX 8000 always run persistent_topk_kernel (opt-in shared memory below 128 KiB); several rows per group when rows outnumber groups | CTA barrier before every arrival and at row end; histogram ring indexed by radix rows only | executed on this branch on V100 and RTX 8000: radix_rows_match (54 cases) passes here and with main's kernel; reused_group passes here and fails with main's kernel | the two races depend on warp scheduling; no deterministic reproducer on V100 or RTX 8000 |
| histogram_2048_topk, k < length <= 8192 | fp32 logits loaded as float4 | row length not a multiple of 4 and fewer than k scores above the fp16 -inf bin | lanes past the row length are never candidates; no effect with finite scores | executed on this branch on V100 and RTX 8000: masked_row_tail 48 passed here, 36 of 48 fail with main's kernel | whether the SM70 indexer scorers produce such rows |
| other persistent_topk paths (trivial rows, histogram_256_topk for 8192 < length <= 32768) and FilteredTopK | fp32 logits | FilteredTopK only with >= 128 KiB opt-in shared memory and more than 32 rows | unchanged | source; -k persistent_topk 153 passed on this branch on V100 and RTX 8000 | FilteredTopK is not reachable on V100 / RTX 8000 |

## Acceleration and benchmark contract (required for performance changes)

- Default enabled or opt-in: always on; bug fix, not a performance change (one CTA barrier per radix round and one per radix row).
- Required CLI options and environment switches: none.
- KV cache dtype used for the benchmark: n/a (no benchmark; not a performance change).
- Wheel SHA or source commit: this branch on main c98a8d664 (C++ change, _C_stable_libtorch must be rebuilt); the same four patches run on our fork (github.com/Peuqui/1Cat-vLLM, fork-main-v6 0b342e7b5).
- PYTHONPATH, source overlays, or external native libraries used: none.
- User-entry route-hit, speed, and output-quality evidence: not a performance change. On our fork, the bundle of 31 upstream backports that contains these four passed an A/B against the same tree without the bundle (logs ab_v6f_dsv4_2026-11-07a.log and ab_v6f_glm_2026-11-07a.log). DeepSeek-V4-Flash PP5 over three V100 and two RTX 8000 (arms T P T P): short decode 55.88 against 55.87 tok/s, GSM8K-30 29 correct in every arm, eight quality texts token-identical, at 486316 prompt tokens first token 145.88 s against 145.90 s and 69.0 ms per decode step in both arms. GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 with DFlash2, PP5 (arms T T P T P): short decode 40.38 to 40.41 tok/s (T) against 40.45 to 40.47 tok/s (P), GSM8K-30 29 correct in every arm, eight quality texts token-identical, at 516196 prompt tokens first token 197.21 s against 197.46 s and 91.7 against 92.9 ms per verify step. These runs show no regression; they are not a reproducer of the four defects.
- Existing kernel/backend registry and capability-rejection reasons: not touched; topk.cu is unchanged.
- Per-engine configuration and deprecated-variable compatibility: no setting added or changed.
- New/changed environment metadata and generated reference check: none.
- Route snapshot command and intentional changed rows: none.
- SM70 registered variables / unregistered reads / model-parameter restrictions, before -> after: no change.

## Test Result

On this branch (main c98a8d664 + these four commits):
- CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py --collect-only: 225 tests, 103 of them new (54 radix_rows_match, 48 masked_row_tail, 1 reused_group). The file needs a GPU, so on CPU only the collection was checked.
- pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: every hook passes, clang-format included; check-layering has no file to check.
- pre-commit run mypy-3.10 --hook-stage manual --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD: passed.
- Tesla V100 and Quadro RTX 8000, each with _C_stable_libtorch rebuilt from this branch: -k "reused_group or radix_rows_match or masked_row_tail" 103 passed; -k persistent_topk 153 passed.
- The same 103 new cases against main's kernel (main c98a8d664 and its own build), on the Tesla V100 and on the Quadro RTX 8000 alike: 37 failed, 66 passed. The 37 are the 36 masked_row_tail cases whose row length is not a multiple of 4 (the count upstream reports for B300) and reused_group_after_short_row (the third row of CTA group 0 returns indices outside the row, e.g. 1065353216). The 54 radix_rows_match cases pass on main's kernel too: the two barrier races did not show on these GPUs, as expected for a race that depends on warp scheduling.

On our fork (the same four patches, fork-main-v6 0b342e7b5 with _C_stable_libtorch rebuilt): -k "reused_group or radix_rows_match or masked_row_tail" 103 passed and -k persistent_topk 153 passed, on a Tesla V100 and on a Quadro RTX 8000.
